rv.q: The entire off-its-rocker off-Broadway show, whose sole sin is occasionally trying too hard, is lovably loony.
Ginger Twinsies is ridiculous, raunchy fun, and for anyone in need of 80 minutes of laughter, the Orpheum Theatre is the place to be.
I laughed at this hailstorm of gags about two-thirds of the time, which, for this type of frolic, is pretty darned good.
Zak’s play succeeds best when he offers his own takes on the details of The Parent Trap’s plot and characters.
Ginger Twinsies skewers a beloved movie with its comic take on the more exaggerated moments of a popular genre, here teen movies and contemporary rom-coms.
That hat alone is, honestly, worth the price of admission.
Otherwise, Zak’s 80 minutes of art by algorithm proves more exhausting than invigorating.
Zak has nudged them to yell every line at the top of their lungs so trippingly on the tongue that any number of his jokes(?) are lost in the gibble-gabble-gargle.
This riotous, joyfully ridiculous romp offers a much-needed dose of laughter.
Kevin Zak's wicked sense of humor and fearless execution make it wholly, deliciously unique.
This is an anarchic ode to the 1998. Disney comedy The Parent Trap, which starred Lindsay Lohan as twins split apart at birth who are reunited at a summer camp in Maine.
Enough funny moments throughout the show for everyone to find something to enjoy.
The jokes and references all zoom by — which is perhaps just as well given that the percentage of punchlines that actually hit the funny bone is relatively low.

cn.t: Critics find this campy Parent Trap parody delivers broad, anarchic laughs for '90s nostalgia fans, though its loud, over-the-top style and relentless pop culture references prove exhausting for some.
